delineation

dih-lin-ee-AY-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Delineation is a precise description or representation of something.

The property survey gave a precise delineation of the boundary, down to the exact bend in the creek.

Example

The zoning map offered a clear delineation of exactly where the residential district ended and the commercial one began.

The map didn't leave any fuzzy edges -- it marked the exact line, which is exactly what makes it a delineation rather than a rough sketch.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

outline: An outline gives the main shape of something — the big sections, the rough plan, the broad strokes — and purposely leaves the small stuff out. A delineation runs the other way: its whole value is exactness, tracing every boundary and detail with precision.

specification: A specification states requirements — the exact standards something must meet, like '2 cm steel, rated for 200 pounds.' A delineation demands nothing: it precisely marks what already exists, showing exactly where one thing ends and another begins.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

vagueness: a lack of clear detail or definition

Where it sits · how exact and detailed it is — description → delineation → blueprint

description vs. delineation: A description can be loose or general; a delineation is specifically precise, often with exact boundaries or details.

blueprint vs. delineation: A blueprint goes a step beyond a delineation: it is a complete technical plan for building something, while a delineation stops at marking boundaries and details precisely.

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: De- ('down/completely') plus line (from Latin linea) plus -ation ('act or process of') gives 'the act of marking out with a line' -- a delineation traces the exact outline or boundary of something.
